Ian Bishop.b:
Ian Bishop enters his third season as assistant swimming coach and recruiting coordinator for Bowling Green in 2026-27.
Bishop followed head coach Tanner Barton to Bowling Green in 2024-25 after two seasons together at Division III John Carroll University, where Bishop also served as assistant coach and recruiting coordinator. He has been part of the Falcons' staff in the program's steady ascent under Barton, including a strong 2025-26 season that saw Bowling Green open 12-0, claim its first MAC dual win since 2022 over Miami (Ohio), defeat Toledo in the Battle of I-75 and helped coach multiple swimmers to top 10 all-time program performances.
At John Carroll, Bishop helped lead the Blue Streaks to two men's and two women's Ohio Athletic Conference championships and was part of four combined OAC Coaching Staff of the Year honors. On both the men's and women's sides, he helped guide three different OAC Swimmer of the Year recipients, nine NCAA Division III Championships qualifiers, six First and Second Team All-Americans and 26 OAC champion swimmers, while the program set seven combined OAC records under his tutelage. As recruiting coordinator, he brought in 31 swimmers and divers over two years, three of whom arrived with incoming times faster than existing program records. In 2024, Bishop was one of six collegiate coaches across all divisions to receive the Collegiate Swimming Coaches Association of America's Jean Freeman Award.
Before John Carroll, Bishop was a volunteer assistant coach at Division III Albion College, helping lead the Britons to third-place finishes at the Michigan Intercollegiate Athletic Association Championships on both the men's and women's sides, and served as head coach of the Parkside Middle School swim team in Jackson, Michigan. Since 2019, he has coached at swim camps for NC State, Georgia, Indiana and Wisconsin, and spent five years as a clinician coach for Wolverine Swim Clinics under former Michigan coach Jim Richardson.
Bishop graduated from Northern Michigan University in 2021 with a bachelor's degree in secondary education and physical education, and earned a master's degree in sports leadership from John Carroll. A former collegiate swimmer, he began his career at Olivet College in sprint freestyle and backstroke before transferring to Northern Michigan, where he competed as a diver before becoming a student assistant coach for his final two seasons.
A native of Jackson, Michigan, Bishop graduated from Jackson High School in 2017, where he also served as an assistant coach in 2021.

Michael Retcher.b:
Michael Retcher enters his fifth season with the Bowling Green swimming and diving program and has helped establish the Falcons as a consistent presence on the conference and national diving scene.
Retcher joined the BGSU staff in 2022 after spending 13 seasons as the head diving coach at Napoleon High School and the Napoleon Diving Club. During his time at Napoleon, 43 student-athletes qualified for the OHSAA State Diving Championships, with 17 finishing in the top 10. He also guided eight divers to NCAA Division I programs and helped 27 Napoleon Diving Club athletes qualify for AAU Nationals, with 12 finishing in the top 12.
Since arriving at Bowling Green, Retcher has continued to build a strong diving tradition while developing a group that has consistently competed at the NCAA Zone level. The Falcons sent four divers to NCAA Zone Diving in each of Retcher’s first two seasons, and in 2025, Natalia Mayorga became the first diver in program history to reach the finals of the NCAA Zone platform competition. Mayorga finished 17th in the platform final, while also placing 24th in the 3-meter event.
Retcher was retained when Tanner Barton was named BGSU’s head coach in 2024, providing continuity as the program entered a new era. Under Barton and Retcher, the Falcons have continued to build on the boards, with Retcher working with a young group that has produced NCAA Zone qualifiers and MAC finalists.
The 2025-26 season produced a significant milestone for Retcher and the Falcons. Mayorga became BGSU’s first MAC champion since 2022 when she won the 3-meter title with a score of 316.85 at the MAC Championships. She earned first-team All-MAC honors and advanced to NCAA Zone C Diving for the third consecutive season.
In addition to his work at BGSU, Retcher has developed an extensive background in diving administration and event management. He currently serves as USA Diving’s director of events and strategic initiatives, where he works on national events and organizational initiatives. He previously served as an AAU National Event Coordinator, running three national qualifying events and overseeing yearly national meets. Retcher also was selected by USA Diving to serve as meet director for the 2022 USA Senior Winter National Championships.
Retcher has also served as president of the Ohio Diving League and as an assistant athletic director at Napoleon High School. He was the head coach of the BGSU Club Water Polo team in 2021-22 and has served as an assistant coach with the Napoleon Water Polo program since 2009.
A 2009 graduate of Napoleon High School, Retcher earned his bachelor’s degree in business administration from Western Governors University in 2023. He is certified as a USA Diving Competition Coach, an AAU Diving Youth Coach and a lifeguard instructor. Before joining the BGSU staff, he also spent seven summers as the assistant waterfront director and kitchen manager at Camp Walden in Cheboygan, Michigan.

Luna Castellanos.b:
Luna Castellanos joins the Bowling Green State University swimming and diving program as an assistant diving coach for the 2026-27 season.
Castellanos comes to Bowling Green after a decorated diving career at Pennsylvania Western University, Clarion, where she served as team captain during the 2025-26 season. An eight-time All-American and five-time national champion, she also earned Scholar All-American honors in 2024 and was named to the Academic All-District Team in both 2025 and 2026.
A double major in psychology and criminal justice, Castellanos graduated with a 3.6 GPA and was a repeat honoree at Clarion's Scholar Athlete Luncheon. Off the boards, she was heavily involved in campus leadership, serving on the Student Athlete Advisory Committee, leading its social media crew and working as a social media assistant for the Clarion diving program throughout her career. She was also a member of the Pennwest Leadership Academy and Eagle Ambassadors.
Castellanos brings coaching experience of her own, having spent multiple summers as a volunteer coach with a club program in Texas and working as a youth diving and Learn to Swim and Dive instructor. Fluent in English and Spanish, she began her college career studying biology at Universidad Javeriana in Cali, Colombia, before transferring to Pennsylvania Western.
Castellanos joins Barton and the Falcons staff ahead of the 2026-27 season.

Tanner Barton.b:
Tanner Barton enters his third season as the head coach of the Bowling Green women's swimming and diving program in 2026-27.
In his first two seasons at BGSU, Barton guided the Falcons to significant progress, highlighted by a historic 2025-26 campaign. Bowling Green finished 13-3 overall and 3-1 in MAC dual meets, marking the program's first winning conference dual-meet record since 2022. The Falcons also opened the season 12-0, the best start in program history, while earning wins over Miami (Ohio) and Eastern Michigan for the first time since the 2015-16 and 2014-15 seasons, respectively. BGSU also captured the Battle of I-75 against Toledo for the first time since 2022.
The Falcons capped the 2025-26 season with their first top-30 finish at the CSCAA National Invitational Championship, placing 30th among 52 teams. BGSU qualified five relays for the meet and had three individual finalists, after having no individual finalists at the NIC the previous season.
Under Barton's leadership, the Falcons have continued to make significant strides in the pool. BGSU has established at least nine new individual top-10 times in program history during his first two seasons, including Emily McNicol's 2:00.15 in the 200-yard backstroke at the 2025 Magnus Cup Invitational.
Barton has also placed an emphasis on the continued development and support of the diving program. During his tenure, BGSU installed new Rough-Tek surfaces on the 5-meter and 7-meter platforms, while three Falcons qualified for NCAA Zone competition in 2025 and four qualified in 2026. Natalia Mayorga capped her junior season by becoming the program's first MAC champion since 2022, winning the 3-meter dive at the 2026 MAC Championships.
Academically, Barton's teams have excelled at a national level. The Falcons have earned CSCAA Academic All-America honors for 16 straight seasons, including each of Barton’s first four semesters at BGSU. His teams have posted the highest team GPA in the MAC each semester, including a 3.77 GPA in fall 2024, a 3.69 in spring 2025, a 3.81 in fall 2025 and a 3.85 in spring 2026. The Falcons earned CSCAA Scholar All-America Team honors in each of those semesters, with their GPAs consistently ranking among the top Division I swimming and diving programs in the country. The 3.77 GPA in fall 2024 ranked seventh nationally among Division I women's programs, while the 3.85 GPA in spring 2026 ranked fourth in the nation.
In Barton's first season at BGSU, the Falcons finished sixth at the 2025 MAC Championships, their best finish at the conference meet since 2022. Ava Vial earned second-team All-MAC honors after finishing third in the 200-yard breaststroke, while the Falcons established multiple new top-10 times in program history.
Barton came to Bowling Green after spending four seasons as the head coach of men's and women's swimming and diving at John Carroll University. During his tenure, he led the Blue Streaks to eight Ohio Athletic Conference championships, including four men's and four women's titles. His teams produced 21 CSCAA first-team All-Americans, 11 CSCAA first-team Scholar All-Americans, 27 OAC records and 104 conference championship titles. His coaching staffs were named OAC Coaching Staff of the Year in each of his four seasons.
Prior to John Carroll, Barton spent one season as the head men's and women's swimming and diving coach at Anderson University in Indiana. He began his collegiate coaching career as a graduate assistant at Ball State during the 2017-18 season.
A native of Dublin, Ohio, Barton graduated summa cum laude from Ball State's Honors College in 2017 with a bachelor's degree in health science and Spanish. He earned a master's degree in exercise science with an emphasis in sport performance from Ball State in 2019 and a Master of Business Administration with a concentration in management and organizational leadership from John Carroll in August 2024.

Greg Zuniga.b:
Greg Zuniga enters his third season on staff with the Bowling Green women's swimming and diving program in 2026-27, serving as an Assistant Coach/Director of Operations.
Zuniga joined the Falcons' staff ahead of head coach Tanner Barton's first season in 2024-25 and has been integral to the program's managment and improvement. He oversaw operational duties and helped coach Bowling Green's 25-26 season. That season, the Falcons opened 12-0, posted its first MAC dual win since 2022 against Miami (Ohio) and defeated Toledo in the Battle of I-75.
Before arriving at Bowling Green, Zuniga spent the 2023-24 season as head coach of the swimming and diving program at Southview High School in Sylvania, Ohio, where he helped the team set new school records and post some of its largest postseason time drops in years. He also served as an assistant coach at Southview during the 2021-22 season, writing practice plans and meet-day lineups while helping send more swimmers to the district meet than the year before.
Zuniga is a Bowling Green graduate, earning his bachelor's degree in intervention specialist studies from the university in 2021. As a student, he served as a student coach/manager for the swimming and diving program from 2018-22, helping run practices and plan team travel.
A native of Massillon, Ohio, Zuniga attended Perry High School before graduating from Canton Central Catholic High School in 2017, where he competed on the swimming and diving team.
